hyps.why: With a tiny learning rate the net is undertrained in 243 epochs, so raising it helps much more than when the rate is already adequate.
At the highest learning rates Adam becomes unstable or diverges, so a further increase hurts compared with lower-rate regions.
Larger batches mean fewer updates per epoch, which compounds undertraining when the learning rate is already small.
More update steps per epoch compensate for a small learning rate, so smaller batches help most there.
Small batches with a high learning rate give noisy, unstable gradients that hurt accuracy relative to the low-rate case.
Strong L2 penalty near 1 causes underfitting, so increasing it further hurts more than at small alpha where it is negligible.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening gives more gain than when the width is already large and saturated.
Deeper nets are more prone to instability at high learning rates, so adding layers hurts more there.
Wider layers speed up fitting per step, which helps when a small learning rate would otherwise leave the model undertrained.
Going from one hidden layer to more adds useful expressiveness, while extra depth beyond two brings diminishing or negative returns.
